findings.evidence: grep 'actions/workflows' scripts/: only resolve_deps.py:159 and mathlib_cache.py:28 query build.yml; both are new in this PR.
findings.fix: Add the query to mathlib_cache.py beside master_build_published (e.g. `newest_master_build(gh, repo)` returning the head_sha of the newest completed successful master-push build.yml run) and have `GitHub.cached_master_tip` call it, so the workflow name, event and success filter exist once.
findings.issue: `GitHub.cached_master_tip` encodes the mathlib cache signal a second time (`actions/workflows/build.yml/runs?branch=master&event=push&status=success`), the exact fact mathlib_cache.py:1 claims as "the one definition for every script" and implements in `_runs`/`master_build_published` (mathlib_cache.py:26-36). The two diverge on failure: if upstream renames build.yml, master_build_published fails closed (check-bump.sh:181 routes to a human) while cached_master_tip's `// empty` silently yields no master candidate and the resolver reports mathlib as merely held back.

findings.evidence: mathlib_cache.py:41 `gh(f"repos/{repo}/compare/{sha}...{BRANCH}", jq=".status").strip() in ("ahead", "identical")` vs resolve_deps.py:309; resolve_deps.py:166-167 passes the module-level `gh`, not `self.compare`.
findings.fix: Keep one predicate: either have `forward` call `mathlib_cache.on_master`, or give `on_master` the compare status so `GitHub.cache_published` can feed it the memoised `self.compare(repo, sha, BRANCH)` result.
findings.issue: `Resolver.forward` tests branch membership with `self.src.compare(self.mathlib_repo, m, self.mathlib_branch)[0] in ("ahead", "identical")`, which is literally `mathlib_cache.on_master` (mathlib_cache.py:39-41) — the resolver already refuses any mathlib rev but `master` (resolve_deps.py:263-266), so the two are the same predicate. Because `on_master` is reached through `cache_published` with the raw `gh` rather than `GitHub.compare`, a release-tag candidate pays the same compare call twice, uncached by the memo, and the recording stores it only inside the opaque `cache_published` answer.

summary: The prior round's four duplications are fixed; lean_versions.py and mathlib_cache.py are genuine shared extractions. What remains is that resolve_deps.py asks two questions mathlib_cache.py was created to own — the master-push build.yml cache signal and master membership — through its own second encoding.
